explanation: Egypt is a warm but conservative society where public displays of affection, including hugging, are generally frowned upon, especially between men and women who are not close relatives. In a social gathering, greetings usually involve a handshake or a light cheek kiss between same-sex acquaintances, so a full hug can feel overly intimate or draw unwanted attention. Waiting for the other person to initiate contact is the safest approach.
local_tip: Offer a handshake first and let your Egyptian host or acquaintance decide whether a cheek kiss or hug is appropriate.
regional_note: Same-sex friends and relatives may exchange hugs or cheek kisses more freely, while mixed-gender hugging is more restricted, particularly in conservative or religious settings.

also_check.note: Hugging is common between same-sex friends but mixed-gender public affection is restrained.
La bise cheek kisses and light hugs among friends are routine greetings.
Bowing is the norm; hugging is uncommon and can feel intrusive in formal greetings.
